message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for my Monopoly turn.

I have $221 and am on Ventnor Avenue. I own three unmortgaged streets plus one house each on Park Place and Boardwalk. The other players are in jail or low on cash.

Player 4 is low on cash and owns purple hotels, railroads, and light blues. I will mortgage Atlantic, Marvin, and Pacific for $420 to fund building two houses on each dark blue. I will not trade or sweeten.

Building two houses on each dark blue costs $400. After mortgaging my three streets I will have $641, leaving $241 after construction. I cannot afford a third house on either property.

Two houses on each dark blue would charge $500 and $600. Player 2 has only $174, so one hit would bankrupt them. Player 4 has just $61, so a hit would likely force liquidation. Player 1 is in jail with $520.

I can only take one action per turn. I will mortgage Pacific first, then the other two streets, to raise enough cash for building.

Mortgaging only two streets would leave $91 after building. Mortgaging all three gives the planned $241 cushion. I am checking exact orange rent values to confirm the threat level.

If I land on New York with three houses, the rent is $600. Selling both houses on Park Place and Boardwalk would raise $400, giving me enough cash to pay without mortgaging the dark blues. Virginia Avenue with three houses is another potential threat.

Virginia Avenue with three houses charges $500, and St. Charles with three charges $450. Player 2 owns both at three houses each. I already rolled and landed on Ventnor, so my next turn will begin from that space.

From Ventnor, rolling a 2 lands on Marvin, a 3 on Go to Jail, and a 4 on Pacific. Rolling a 5 would land on North Carolina, but since Player 4's Pennsylvania is mortgaged, that street charges only the base rent of $26.

The next roll from Ventnor is safe. The nearest opponent properties are far away. I will pass the light blues, orange, and pink monopolies on my next lap.

Player 4 is next in line after me. They are on Chance with only $61, so they could not afford a one-house rent on my Park Place. I will mortgage the three streets and build two houses before their turn begins.

I rejected a trade for Ventnor Avenue because Player 4 refused to sell it cheaply. A yellow monopoly would be huge, but I cannot afford to build there while keeping my dark blue houses.

Player 4 wants Pacific Avenue to complete their green monopoly. That would be catastrophic, so I will not trade it. Trades with Player 1 or Player 2 offer no useful pieces. Building two houses on each dark blue is the only viable path.

Mortgaging Pacific Avenue is the better choice. Player 4 does not own a complete green monopoly, so the $26 base rent is negligible. The $150 cash raised is more valuable than the rent for building and as a safety cushion. Keeping only two streets mortgaged would leave just $91 after construction, which is too thin to handle unexpected expenses.

I will mortgage Atlantic Avenue first. I am keeping my message brief and strategic.
